name: Cloud & Infrastructure
oneLiner: Turns racks of chips into rentable, schedulable clusters for training and serving models.

analogy.text: A utility company: you plug in and pay for what you use, without owning the power plant.
analogy.breaks: Unlike electricity, AI capacity isn't interchangeable: specific chips, network layouts and regions matter, and capacity can simply be unavailable.

givesAbove: On-demand clusters, storage and networking that teams can train and serve models on.
needsBelow: Accelerators and interconnect from Compute Hardware, housed and powered by Physical & Energy.

walkthrough.title: Chips wired into one machine
walkthrough.text: A lab wants to train a new model. Thousands of accelerators are linked by a fast network fabric so they can share results every step.

walkthrough.title: Renting the cluster
walkthrough.text: The lab doesn't own that cluster. It rents it from a GPU cloud, reserving capacity for the weeks the run will take.

walkthrough.title: Training, then serving
walkthrough.text: Once trained, the model moves from one giant training job to many small serving copies, sized for fast, cheap answers.

walkthrough.title: Or run it at home
walkthrough.text: If the weights are released, a hobbyist can download a quantised version and run it on their own machine instead of renting.
